chunks: Ali ibn Mahziyar from al-Hasan from Ibn Abi Umayr from Umar ibn Udhaynah from Zurarah from al-Fudayl who said:

I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: 'Complete it [the prayer] during the day while the sun is odd [i.e., before sunset], and when the sun sets, it is even [i.e., the time for the evening prayer begins].'.

key_terms.مَثْنَى: Even (referring to the time after sunset)
key_terms.وَتْراً: Odd (referring to the time before sunset)

ai.seo_question: When should the Maghrib prayer be performed according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the precise temporal boundary for Maghrib prayer, distinguishing between the 'odd' period of sunset visibility and the 'even' period after the sun has fully set. It reflects the Shia juristic emphasis on the immediate performance of Maghrib before the onset of the next prayer's time, ensuring the prayer is offered within its designated window of obligation.
